Following is the exact implementation requirnment for an web protal.

**Context**

When goods are imported into the US, a licensed customs broker files an entry with CBP describing the shipment: what it is, where it came from, what it's worth, and who's involved. Brokers prepare these entries in filing software, and NetCHB is one of the most widely used. At Sefer, we turn raw shipping documents into entries that are ready to file.

**The task**

Build a simple web app where a user uploads the documents for a shipment and gets back a NetCHB-ready entry, along with any additional information or steps needed to complete it.

Attached (under Data) are the documents for one shipment (a commercial invoice, packing list, and bill of lading) to build and test with. To get there, you'll need to:

1. Extract the relevant data from the documents.
2. Figure out what NetCHB expects. NetCHB has an XML web service. Find it, locate the entry XML, and work out its structure.
3. Generate the entry XML for the uploaded shipment and display it in the app.

Your app should work for other shipments too, not just this one. We'll test it with documents you haven't seen.

The app must be written in Typescript use pnpm package manager and it must have lightweight frontend and the whole app can be hostable easily so first create a plan of action \shipping-docs contains the sample documents

1\. If a description is used that matches our internal list of generic descriptions, we will give a warning to update the description to be more specific. (e.g. Items would be a generic description that CBP might flag) 

  
2\. If a description is used for multiple different HTS codes in the upload, our system will throw a warning to make each tariff have a unique description.

## Getting Started with v2 (Coming from v1) ```js // v1 // const pdf = require('pdf-parse'); // pdf(buffer).then(result => console.log(result.text)); // v2 const { PDFParse } = require('pdf-parse'); // import { PDFParse } from 'pdf-parse'; async function run() { const parser = new PDFParse({ url: 'https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf' }); const result = await parser.getText(); console.log(result.text); } run(); ``` ## Features - CJS, ESM, Node.js, and browser support. - Can be integrated with `React`, `Vue`, `Angular`, or any other web framework. - **Command-line interface** for quick PDF processing: [`CLI Documentation`](./docs/command-line.md) - [`Security Policy`](https://github.com/mehmet-kozan/pdf-parse?tab=security-ov-file#security-policy) - Retrieve headers and validate PDF : [`getHeader`](#getheader--node-utility-pdf-header-retrieval-and-validation) - Extract document info : [`getInfo`](#getinfo--extract-metadata-and-document-information) - Extract page text : [`getText`](#gettext--extract-text) - Render pages as PNG : [`getScreenshot`](#getscreenshot--render-pages-as-png) - Extract embedded images : [`getImage`](#getimage--extract-embedded-images) - Detect and extract tabular data : [`getTable`](#gettable--extract-tabular-data) - Well-covered with [`unit tests`](./tests) - [`Integration tests`](./tests/integration) to validate end-to-end behavior across environments. - See [LoadParameters](./docs/options.md#load-parameters) and [ParseParameters](./docs/options.md#parse-parameters) for all available options. - Examples: [`live demo`](./reports/demo/), [`examples`](./examples/), [`tests`](./tests/unit/) and [`tests example`](./tests/unit/test-example/) folders. - Supports: [`Next.js + Vercel`](https://github.com/mehmet-kozan/vercel-next-app-demo), Netlify, AWS Lambda, Cloudflare Workers. ## Installation ```sh npm install pdf-parse # or pnpm add pdf-parse # or yarn add pdf-parse # or bun add pdf-parse ``` ### CLI Installation For command-line usage, install the package globally: ```sh npm install -g pdf-parse ``` Or use it directly with npx: ```sh npx pdf-parse --help ``` For detailed CLI documentation and usage examples, see: [CLI Documentation](./docs/command-line.md) ## Usage ### `getHeader` — Node Utility: PDF Header Retrieval and Validation ```js // Important: getHeader is available from the 'pdf-parse/node' submodule import { getHeader } from 'pdf-parse/node'; // Retrieve HTTP headers and file size without downloading the full file. // Pass `true` to check PDF magic bytes via range request. // Optionally validates PDFs by fetching the first 4 bytes (magic bytes). // Useful for checking file existence, size, and type before full parsing. // Node only, will not work in browser environments. const result = await getHeader('https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf', true); console.log(`Status: ${result.status}`); console.log(`Content-Length: ${result.size}`); console.log(`Is PDF: ${result.isPdf}`); console.log(`Headers:`, result.headers); ``` ### `getInfo` — Extract Metadata and Document Information ```js import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises'; import { PDFParse } from 'pdf-parse'; const link = 'https://mehmet-kozan.github.io/pdf-parse/pdf/climate.pdf'; // const buffer = await readFile('reports/pdf/climate.pdf'); // const parser = new PDFParse({ data: buffer }); const parser = new PDFParse({ url: link }); const result = await parser.getInfo({ parsePageInfo: true }); await parser.destroy(); console.log(`Total pages: ${result.total}`); console.log(`Title: ${result.info?.Title}`); console.log(`Author: ${result.info?.Author}`); console.log(`Creator: ${result.info?.Creator}`); console.log(`Producer: ${result.info?.Producer}`); // Access parsed date information const dates = result.getDateNode(); console.log(`Creation Date: ${dates.CreationDate}`); console.log(`Modification Date: ${dates.ModDate}`); // Links, pageLabel, width, height (when `parsePageInfo` is true) console.log('Per-page information:'); console.log(JSON.stringify(result.pages, null, 2)); ``` ### `getText` — Extract Text ```js import { PDFParse } from 'pdf-parse'; const parser = new PDFParse({ url: 'https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf' }); const result = await parser.getText(); // to extract text from page 3 only: // const result = await parser.getText({ partial: [3] }); await parser.destroy(); console.log(result.text); ``` For a complete list of configuration options, see: - - Value

- Conflicting alternatives

- Parties and addresses
- Transport and routing
- Bills of lading and containers
- Invoices and currencies

### 1. `libxml2-wasm`
- **Library:** [`libxml2-wasm`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/libxml2-wasm)
- **What is it?** This package wraps libxml2, compiled to WebAssembly, for fast, standards-compliant XML/XSD parsing and validation, with strong compatibility for modern browsers and Node.js.
- **Browser support:** Chrome v89+, Edge v89+, Safari v15+, Node.js v18+
- **Features:** Parsing, querying, validating (including XSD), modifying XML; supports includes/imports (experimental).
- **Installation:** `npm install libxml2-wasm`
- **Docs & Example:** See [official documentation and examples](https://jameslan.github.io/libxml2-wasm/index.html).
- **How to use for validation:**
  ```js
  import { XmlDocument } from 'libxml2-wasm';
  const doc = XmlDocument.fromString('<your-xml-here>');
  const xsd = XmlDocument.fromString('<your-xsd-schema-here>');
  const isValid = doc.validate(xsd);
  doc.dispose(); xsd.dispose();
  ```

- **Library:** [`xmllint-wasm`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/xmllint-wasm)

# libxml2-wasm

[![CI Build on master](https://github.com/jameslan/libxml2-wasm/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jameslan/libxml2-wasm/actions/workflows/build.yml)

# Why Choose Another XML Library?

When comparing the previous two main approaches —
pure JavaScript implementation and traditional C implementation binding —
WebAssembly offers a unique combination of advantages.
It provides excellent performance while maintaining the best compatibility with modern JavaScript runtimes.

|                               | Javascript Implementation |       Traditional C Binding        |    WebAssembly    |
|-------------------------------|:-------------------------:|:----------------------------------:|:-----------------:|
| Parsing Speed                 |        Average[^1]        |                Fast                |       Fast        |
| C/C++ Toolchain at Runtime    |       Not required        |            Required[^2]            |   Not Required    |
| Prebuilt Binaries             |            N/A            |  One for each OS / Runtime / Arch  | Universal for all |
| Prebuilt Binary Compatibility |            N/A            | May be broken across libc versions |     Very Good     |
| Browser Compatibility         |            Yes            |                 No                 |        Yes        |

## Documentation

https://jameslan.github.io/libxml2-wasm/index.html

# Supported Environments

Due to the usage of WebAssembly, ES module and [top level await](https://caniuse.com/?search=top%20level%20await) etc,
this library requires the minimum version of the following environments,

| Environment |Version|
|:-----------:|:---:|
|   Node.js   |v18+|
|   Chrome    |V89+|
|    Edge     |V89+|
|   Safari    |v15+|

# Features
- Parsing & Querying
- Validating
- Modifying
- Serializing
- XInclude and XSD include/import (experimental)

## Getting started

Install `libxml2-wasm` package:

```shell
npm i libxml2-wasm
```

`libxml2-wasm` is an ES module,
the import process differs between ES modules and CommonJS modules.

### From ES Module

```js
import fs from 'node:fs';
import { XmlDocument } from 'libxml2-wasm';
const doc1 = XmlDocument.fromString('<note><to>Tove</to></note>');
const doc2 = XmlDocument.fromBuffer(fs.readFileSync('doc.xml'));
doc1.dispose();
doc2.dispose();
```

### From CommonJS

```js
const fs = require('node:fs');
import('libxml2-wasm').then(({ XmlDocument }) => {
    const doc1 = XmlDocument.fromString('<note><to>Tove</to></note>');
    const doc2 = XmlDocument.fromBuffer(fs.readFileSync('doc.xml'));
    doc1.dispose();
    doc2.dispose();
});
```

**IMPORTANT**: `dispose()` is required to avoid memory leak.

For more detail, see the [Doc](https://jameslan.github.io/libxml2-wasm/index.html).

# NetCHB Shipment Entry Portal — Implementation Plan

## Objective

Build a lightweight TypeScript web application that accepts shipment documents, extracts shipment data with AI, lets the user review and correct it, and produces XSD-valid NetCHB entry XML.

The supplied commercial invoice, packing list, and bill of lading are test fixtures only. Extraction must work with unfamiliar document layouts and combinations of PDFs and images.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Document upload] --> B[AI extraction]
    B --> C[Normalized shipment JSON]
    C --> D[User review and edit]
    D --> E[Deterministic NetCHB XML]
    E --> F[XSD validation]
    F --> G[Display and download]
```

## Technology

- TypeScript and pnpm
- Vite with a lightweight frontend
- Zod for validating extracted and edited shipment JSON
- A multimodal AI provider for document extraction
- A deterministic XML builder
- An XSD validator using the official NetCHB schemas
- No database, Docker, or rules engine

## Processing Pipeline

### 1. Document upload

- Accept multiple shipment documents in one upload.
- Support text and scanned PDFs plus common image formats.
- Enforce file count, type, and size limits at the API boundary.
- Keep uploaded data transient and avoid logging document contents.

### 2. AI extraction

- Extract embedded PDF text where available.
- Send scanned pages and images to a multimodal model.
- Ask the model for JSON matching the canonical shipment schema.
- Require `null` for unavailable values instead of inferred or invented defaults.
- Validate every AI response with Zod before using it.
- Return a recoverable error when extraction output cannot be validated.

### 3. Normalized shipment JSON

Keep the canonical model small and limited to fields needed for the supplied shipment and likely test shipments:

- Importer, consignee, seller, and manufacturer
- Invoice number, date, currency, and Incoterm
- Processing port, entry port, port of loading, and port of discharge
- Vessel, voyage, bill of lading, container numbers, and arrival date
- Entry type, bond type, entry date, packages, gross weight, freight, insurance, and assists
- Invoice lines containing description, country of origin, HTS code, quantity, unit, value, and manufacturer

Extracted fields use a simple wrapper:

```typescript
type ExtractedField<T> = {
  value: T | null;
  confidence: number;
  source?: {
    document: string;
    page?: number;
  };
};
```

Obvious conflicts are represented as a small list containing the field path and competing values. A generalized provenance or customs rules engine is out of scope.

### 4. User review and edit

Present one editable review screen that:

- Shows all normalized shipment fields.
- Highlights low-confidence values.
- Lists missing required fields.
- Shows obvious conflicts across documents.
- Allows invoice lines to be added, edited, or removed.
- Allows users to enter broker or customs data absent from the documents.

Empty optional NetCHB fields remain omitted. The application must not manufacture missing information.

### 5. Deterministic NetCHB XML generation

Generate XML from reviewed JSON using TypeScript, never AI. The renderer must:

- Map canonical fields to NetCHB elements.
- Preserve the element order required by the NetCHB XSD.
- Escape text safely.
- Format dates, quantities, identifiers, and monetary values correctly.
- Omit empty optional elements.
- Report missing compulsory values before rendering.

Automatic transmission to NetCHB or CBP is not included.

### 6. XSD validation

- Bundle the official NetCHB entry XSD and its dependent datatype schema.
- Validate every generated XML document.
- Show validation errors clearly, including the affected element or path when available.
- Preserve reviewed JSON after a validation failure so the user can correct it.
- Enable XML download only after successful XSD validation.

### 7. Display and download

The result screen will show:

- Readiness and XSD validation status
- Formatted XML
- Validation errors, if any
- Copy XML action
- Download XML action

## Progress States

Use a simple stage-based status indicator:

1. Uploading
2. Reading documents
3. Extracting shipment data
4. Validating extracted data
5. Ready for review
6. Generating XML
7. Validating XML
8. Complete or failed

No percentage estimation or background job system is required for the initial implementation.

## Suggested Project Structure

```text
src/
  api/
    extract.ts
    generate.ts
  components/
    UploadForm.ts
    ReviewForm.ts
    ResultView.ts
    StageStatus.ts
  lib/
    extraction.ts
    shipment-schema.ts
    conflicts.ts
    netchb-renderer.ts
    xsd-validator.ts
  schemas/
    entry.xsd
    data_type.xsd
  main.ts
  styles.css
tests/
  fixtures/
  shipment-schema.test.ts
  netchb-renderer.test.ts
  xsd-validation.test.ts
```

The exact structure may be reduced while implementing if fewer files remain clear.

## Implementation Sequence

1. Scaffold the pnpm TypeScript/Vite application.
2. Add the official NetCHB schemas.
3. Define the small Zod shipment model.
4. Implement document upload and stage status UI.
5. Implement multimodal AI extraction and response validation.
6. Build the editable review form with confidence, missing-field, and conflict indicators.
7. Implement the deterministic NetCHB XML renderer.
8. Add XSD validation and clear error display.
9. Add formatted XML display, copy, and download actions.
10. Test with the supplied shipment and additional varied fixtures.

## Validation Strategy

- Canonical JSON schema tests
- Invalid AI response tests
- Missing-field and low-confidence display tests
- Basic conflict detection tests
- XML ordering, omission, and escaping tests
- XSD-valid and XSD-invalid XML tests
- End-to-end upload, review, generate, validate, and download test
- Regression fixture using the supplied shipment documents

## Acceptance Criteria

- Multiple unfamiliar shipment documents can be uploaded together.
- AI output is normalized and schema-validated before display.
- Missing information remains empty rather than hallucinated.
- Users can review and correct extracted values.
- Confidence, required missing fields, and obvious conflicts are visible.
- XML generation is deterministic and follows NetCHB element ordering.
- Generated XML is validated against the official NetCHB XSD.
- Validation errors are understandable and actionable.
- Valid XML can be displayed, copied, and downloaded.
